title: AI for Sales and Product Consulting

questions.question: What is the main risk of AI-generated customer-facing material?
options: It shifts preparation work from the account team over to the product consultant
It keeps proposal drafts internal so they never reach the stakeholder review step
It can invent customer context, overstate value, and weaken trust when unchecked
It slows discovery preparation because every competitive note has to be rewritten
questions.explanation: The lesson's problem statement is that a polished output invents context, overstates value, or weakens trust. Customer-facing material therefore needs an evidence check and a review before it is shared.

questions.question: A proposal draft reads well, but nobody can say where its customer numbers came from. Which control of this lesson addresses that?
options: The follow-up plan, which records the customer action expected after the meeting
The source check, which confirms every customer claim traces back to real context
The value story, which shapes how the benefit is framed for the customer audience during the pitch
The stakeholder review, which puts a second reader on the draft before it is sent
questions.explanation: Unattributed numbers are an evidence problem, and the source check is the control that ties each claim back to actual customer context. Value story, stakeholder review, and follow-up plan are the other three controls the lesson teaches.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A finished customer proposal that can be sent externally without further review
A competitive analysis that replaces the team's own customer discovery interviews
A CRM record set that tracks every follow-up action assigned during the meeting
A ranked sales and product consulting AI plan with controls and a rationale each
questions.explanation: The artifact triages customer context and maps signals such as proposal risk to control levels, so teams can choose the controls before AI-assisted material is shared.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A proposal claim that skips the source check so the draft can go out the same day
A value story written from the model's assumptions rather than customer context
A follow-up list kept private to the author, so the customer only sees the proposal
A stakeholder review that puts a second reader on material before it is shared
questions.explanation: Stakeholder review protects customer trust. Source check, value story, and follow-up plan are the other three controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should customer-facing AI material require stronger controls?
options: Only when the draft stays internal and no customer will read the final version
Only when the follow-up plan is already written down and assigned to a named owner
Never, because a polished draft with a clear value story is evidence enough already
When proposal risk is high, customer evidence is weak, or the impact is large
questions.explanation: Proposal risk and weak customer signal are exactly the inputs the triage artifact maps to a stronger control level, and high-impact external material carries the most trust at stake.

questions.question: What should AI improve in sales and product consulting?
options: The number of customer claims a proposal makes without a source check behind them
The speed of sending material externally by dropping the stakeholder review step
Preparation quality, the clarity of the value story, and follow-up discipline
The volume of competitive notes produced, whatever customer context is available
questions.explanation: The lesson positions AI as support for preparation: sharper customer context, a clearer value hypothesis, and follow-up discipline that turns preparation into better customer action.
